requirement: Thin drivers invoke identical application behavior

files.note: Byte-identical to project_gdunit4's copy -- confirmed via matching sha256, not merely 'the same by construction'.

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: check.py -> real GUT v9.7.1 run (project_gut) and real GdUnit4 v6.2.1 run (project_gdunit4), each a thin wrapper calling subject.gd:run(3, log) then run(-1, log) and writing the resulting log+results to its own user://trace.json

measured_with_gut_9_7_1_and_gdunit4_6_2_.finding: The two runners' thin test wrappers, driving byte-identical subject.gd source with the same inputs, produce a byte-for-byte identical event trace. Neither runner's own test-execution machinery (assertion style, suite discovery, reporting) alters the application code's own observable behavior in any way -- exactly the requirement, confirmed by direct file comparison rather than eyeballing similar-looking output.

notes: The trace is written to user://trace.json, not stdout -- GUT and GdUnit4 format console output completely differently (GdUnit4's is ANSI-colored and structured very differently from GUT's), so comparing stdout would diff runner presentation noise, not application behavior. Each project has its own project.godot with a distinct config/name (per F076's established isolation fact), so each runner's trace lands in its own separate app_userdata directory and check.py reads each one back by its own absolute path. Two separate real end-to-end runs (GUT via addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd, GdUnit4 via addons/gdUnit4/runtest.sh), following the F080-appropriate variant of the one-input-one-measured-run rule: this fixture's single 'input' legitimately spans two runs because the requirement is explicitly a CROSS-RUNNER comparison, not a claim about either run's coverage state in isolation (contrast with F041/F044/F048, where two runs would have falsely conflated cumulative-report state).
author: godot-tooling-session-2026-09-19
reviewer: independent review agent (fable), 2026-09-19: re-hashed all five bound files, confirmed the two subject.gd copies are byte-identical and that run(3)/run(-1) yield 6/0 with the recorded log by reading the source; re-ran check.py (real GUT and real GdUnit4 runs), traces byte-identical. Nothing to correct.
ambiguities: This fixture establishes APPLICATION BEHAVIOR parity, not gd-tools COVERAGE parity across runners -- gd-tools' coverage collection is bound to GUT's own hook system (pre_run_hook.gd/post_run_hook.gd, see F081's oracle), and was not invoked in the GdUnit4 run at all here. Whether a gd-tools coverage measurement of the GdUnit4 run (e.g. via F081's manual-driver technique, adapted to GdUnit4's own execution model) would match the GUT-measured coverage for the same subject.gd is a materially different, unbuilt question -- explicitly out of this fixture's scope, not silently assumed.

Only a simple RefCounted subject with no scene-tree dependency is exercised. Parity for a lifecycle-domain-style subject (autoloads, signals, scene tree) that behaves differently under each runner's own scene/process setup is untested.
